subject: Artera onboarding — evidence request, DPIA workshop and transfer assurances
messages:
From: James O'Neill <procurement@arterahealth.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Singh <m.singh@arterahealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Artera onboarding — evidence & DPIA support needed

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Artera's info‑sec and procurement teams are progressing the onboarding checklist. Before we can move to legal review of the DPA, security needs a compact evidence bundle and a short DPIA workshop to validate controls for the pilot. Can you provide the following by COB 2026‑03‑25?

- Article 28 register extract (export showing subprocessors, purpose categories, and EU/US region for each)
- Article 30 processing activities summary for the Redwood service used by Artera (CSV preferred)
- KMS/HSM attestation or key custody statement (who controls keys — Redwood, customer-managed, or hybrid?)
- Recent access‑log extract (redacted example) showing admin access and principal names for March 2026
- DPIA workbook or questionnaire you typically use when onboarding regulated healthcare customers
- Any transfer mechanism summaries (SCCs, BCRs, or binding legal instruments) applicable to US↔EU flows
- Confirmation of retention default and how to request deletions for test data

Also: our security lead (Maya) would like a 60‑minute DPIA workshop next week to review the flows and evidence. Do you have availability 2026‑03‑18 or 2026‑03‑19 (US Pacific)?

We may need example language for the DPA about supplier audit rights — please highlight what you can provide (in‑person audit, remote evidence portal, sampling approach).

Thanks — if it's easier I can share a short form that lists exactly the bits our supplier review requires and we can tick boxes off.

— James
James O'Neill
Head of Procurement, Artera Health
procurement@arterahealth.com

Hi James / Maya —

Thanks — great to see Artera moving forward. We're happy to support the evidence request and run a DPIA workshop. I've looped in Neha (privacy operations) and Laura (legal) so they can own the artifacts and timelines.

Short plan:
- I'll upload an initial evidence packet today (attachments below) that contains a draft Art.30 CSV, our current subprocessor register extract, and a KMS/HSM attestation stub.
- Neha will prepare a redacted sample of access logs (March) and our DPIA workbook for the workshop.
- Laura will respond on audit rights language and options (remote evidence portal vs on‑site).

Workshop availability: 2026‑03‑18 @ 10:00 PT or 2026‑03‑19 @ 14:00 PT — please confirm which works.

Deliverables I will attach in the next email: redwood_art30_register_v1.csv, redwood_dpia_workbook.xlsx, kms_hsm_attestation_2026-02.pdf, initial-evidence-packet.zip. If Artera has a supplier form (like the PDF you attached) we can map responses directly.

We'll also include links to our transfer instruments and the HubSpot deal for tracking.

Talk soon —

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-16T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Artera evidence — quick review notes

Tessa / Neha —

I reviewed James' list and the packet Tessa is preparing. A few notes for the packet and for the workshop:

1) Subprocessor detail: we should provide purpose categories and indicate whether any subprocessor ever handles unredacted health data. For the analytics subprocessor (EdgeCache Labs) confirm storage region and whether they perform ephemeral caching only or persistent storage.

2) KMS: we have two modes — customer‑managed keys via our KMS integration (customer retains control) and Redwood default keys (we manage). The attestation should clearly state which is in use for Artera and whether HSM is used for key wrapping. Provide kms_hsm_attestation_2026-02.pdf.

3) Access logs: provide a redacted CSV sample (admin+operator actions) and an explanation of retention/aggregation windows. Redact PII but keep principal roles.

4) Audit rights: for customers on enterprise contracts we offer remote evidence and time‑boxed sampling for on‑site audits. We should outline options (remote portal + curated exports, 1 on‑site per year with NDA, or SOC2 + targeted evidence). I can draft a paragraph for the DPA.

5) Cross‑border: include our standard SCCs summary (we rely on clause flow and DP compatibility mapping) and note our planned mitigations (encryption‑in‑transit, at‑rest encryption, and regional tenant pinning where available).

I'll draft the audit clause and attach a short FAQ for the workshop.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
From: James O'Neill <procurement@arterahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <m.singh@arterahealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-17T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Artera onboarding — evidence & DPIA support needed

Tessa — thanks for the quick response and loop‑in. A couple of clarifying questions ahead of the workshop:

1) For the KMS modes, can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer‑managed master keys (CMK) where Artera's KMS holds the root key material (i.e., Redwood never sees unwrapped keys)? If yes, which cloud KMS providers are supported and is there guidance for bringing keys from an on‑prem HSM?

2) For SCCs/BCRs: will you be sending a copy or a short one‑page summary of the transfer mechanism you intend to rely on? We need this for our legal intake.

3) For the sample access logs: please include an example showing the fields you will export (timestamp, actor_role, action, resource_id, requester_ip). A single redacted CSV is fine.

4) Audit logistics: we prefer remote evidence via a secure portal and sampling exports rather than an on‑site by default. Please confirm that remote evidence is acceptable and provide your expected turnaround (e.g., 3 business days after request).

5) DocuSign for the DPA: please send the DPA link when ready.

If you can attach the CSV and KMS attestation now, we can run those through our intake before the workshop.

Thanks —
James

James / Maya —

Attached are the items we discussed. See notes inline below. If anything needs further redaction or expansion ahead of the workshop, say so and we will iterate quickly.

Attachments (zipped and individual files):
- redwood_art30_register_v1.csv — Article 30 processing activities (summary columns: activity_id, purpose, data_categories, legal_basis, subprocessors_involved, region)
- redwood_dpia_workbook.xlsx — DPIA workbook with flow diagrams and control mapping (workshop will walk through this)
- kms_hsm_attestation_2026-02.pdf — statement of HSM usage and supported CMK modes (cloud KMS: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault; on‑prem HSM bring‑your‑own supported via key import guidance)
- sample-access-logs-202603.csv — redacted example with fields: timestamp, actor_role, action, resource_id, requester_ip (IPs masked)
- initial-evidence-packet.zip — contains the above plus a short FAQ and our SCCs one‑page summary

Quick answers to your questions:
1) CMK: yes — Artera may elect customer‑managed keys. When CMK is selected, Redwood does not have access to unwrapped root key material. We support AWS KMS (Customer managed CMK), GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. We also have guidance for importing keys from on‑prem HSMs; see the KMS attestation for the exact text.

2) Transfer mechanisms: included is a one‑page SCCs summary from our legal team. For enterprise contracts we can provide clause text and a tailored summary for Artera's country list.

3) Access logs: sample attached. Full exports are available via our evidence portal; typical turnaround is 3 business days for ad‑hoc requests (we can include this in the DPA).

4) Remote evidence: we support a secure evidence portal with curated exports and audits. We are happy to default to remote evidence + sampling as you requested; on‑site remains an option under enterprise terms.

5) DocuSign: I'm preparing the DPA package; I'll send the DocuSign link by end of day tomorrow.

Workshop: 2026‑03‑18 @ 10:00 PT is confirmed. I'll send a calendar invite with a short agenda and the workbook as pre‑reads.

Next steps: please review the attachments. Laura will follow up with audit clause language and Neha will own the DPIA facilitation.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555‑0142
E: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
